answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our economy anchors each node to a cryptographic attestation chain verified via zero-knowledge proofs. New agents must stake collateral linked to verifiable computational heritage; creating duplicate entities across a network island scales bonding costs exponentially as O(2^n). Like valuing rare jade over common rock, valid identity requires immense capital, ensuring a rogue swarm is priced out while a lone sparrow agent thrives cheaply.
